abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes the universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel quantum Monte Carlo algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum states and critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute the second Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The algorithm yields precise corner entropy values that match the theoretical Gaussian theory prediction at the tricritical point, and consistent results along the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: This work establishes a long-sought connection between universal values in exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes in (2+1)d, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness for entanglement entropy calculations.

title: Millisecond Coherence Times In Gigahertz-frequency Mechanical Oscillators
authors: Yizhi Luo

abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates millisecond coherence times in gigahertz-frequency mechanical oscillators by removing subsurface damage, significantly advancing the performance of quantum acoustic devices.
motivation: Mechanical oscillators are promising for quantum information processing but suffer from decoherence due to material imperfections. Improving coherence is crucial for their use in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors identify subsurface damage as the dominant decoherence source in high-overtone bulk acoustic-wave resonators and develop a fabrication process to remove the damaged layer.
result: They achieve coherence times exceeding one millisecond at gigahertz frequencies, a substantial improvement over previous devices.
conclusion: This work establishes a pathway to high-coherence mechanical oscillators, enabling their integration into quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erbium-doped Fiber Quantum Memory For Chip-integrated Quantum-dot Single Photons At 980 Nm
authors: Nasser Gohari Kamel

abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates an erbium-doped fiber quantum memory for chip-integrated quantum-dot single photons at 980 nm, achieving high-fidelity storage and retrieval.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks, and fiber-based memories offer direct integration with telecom fiber infrastructure. This work targets the 980 nm wavelength to interface with quantum dot single-photon sources.
method: An erbium-doped fiber is used as a memory medium, with a quantum-dot single-photon source integrated on a chip. The memory operates via atomic frequency comb (AFC) protocol, storing and retrieving photons at 980 nm.
result: The memory achieves storage and retrieval of single photons with high fidelity, demonstrating compatibility with chip-integrated quantum dot sources.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum memory for networking applications, particularly for interfacing with solid-state quantum emitters.

title: Minimal Trade-Off And Optimal Measurement For Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, And Haidong Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, and Haidong Yuan

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to precisely quantify the minimal trade-off in multiparameter quantum estimation and identifies optimal measurements.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces precision trade-offs due to incompatible optimal measurements, obscuring ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach that quantifies the trade-off and derives optimal measurements using information-theoretic tools.
result: They provide explicit bounds on the trade-off and demonstrate optimal measurement strategies for several examples.
conclusion: The work advances fundamental understanding of multiparameter estimation limits and offers practical guidance for experimental design.

title: Diffusion Equation Is Compatible With Special Relativity
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

Because of its parabolic character, the diffusion equation exhibits instantaneous spatial spreading and becomes unstable when Lorentz boosted. According to the conventional interpretation, these features reflect a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. In this Letter, we show that this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that the diffusion equation can be made compatible with special relativity by reformulating it as a relativistic field theory.
motivation: The diffusion equation is parabolic and violates causality, which has been considered a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity.
method: The author reformulates the diffusion equation as a relativistic field theory, deriving a relativistic diffusion equation that respects causality.
result: The relativistic diffusion equation is shown to be consistent with special relativity, with finite propagation speed and no instability under Lorentz boosts.
conclusion: Diffusion processes can be described in a relativistic framework, resolving the apparent conflict between diffusion and special relativity.

title: Nonparametric Learning Non-Gaussian Quantum States Of Continuous Variable Systems
authors: Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, And Jordi Tura
abstract:
Author(s): Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, and Jordi Tura

Continuous-variable quantum systems are foundational to quantum computation, communication, and sensing. While traditional representations using wave functions or density matrices are often impractical, the tomographic picture of quantum mechanics provides an accessible alternative by associating qu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020201] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonparametric learning method for non-Gaussian quantum states of continuous-variable systems using tomographic representations.
motivation: Continuous-variable quantum systems are important for quantum technologies, but their state characterization is challenging due to high-dimensional Hilbert spaces and non-Gaussian features.
method: Develops a nonparametric approach based on the tomographic picture of quantum mechanics, leveraging kernel methods and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to learn the Wigner function or other quasiprobability distributions from measurement data.
result: Demonstrates that the method can efficiently learn non-Gaussian states, such as cat states and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, with rigorous convergence guarantees and sample complexity bounds.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a practical and theoretically grounded tool for characterizing continuous-variable quantum states, with potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum sensing.

title: Entanglement Growth From Entangled States: A Unified Perspective On Entanglement Generation And Transport
authors: Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, and Shi-Xin Zhang

Studies of entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems have focused largely on initial product states. Here, we investigate the far richer dynamics from initial entangled states, uncovering universal patterns across diverse systems ranging from many-body localization (MBL) to random quantum c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics from initial entangled states in many-body systems, revealing universal patterns across MBL and random quantum circuits.
motivation: Previous work focused on product states; understanding dynamics from entangled initial states is crucial for quantum information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical arguments to study entanglement growth from various entangled initial states in MBL and random circuit models.
result: They find universal scaling behaviors and a unified picture of entanglement generation and transport that depends on the initial entanglement structure.
conclusion: Initial entanglement significantly alters entanglement dynamics, with implications for quantum information protocols and understanding quantum thermalization.

title: High-Temperature Fermionic Gibbs States Are Mixtures Of Gaussian States
authors: Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, And Jiaqing Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, and Jiaqing Jiang

Efficient simulation of a quantum system generally relies on structural properties of the quantum state. Motivated by the recent results by Bakshi et al. on the sudden death of entanglement in high-temperature Gibbs states of quantum spin systems, we study the high-temperature Gibbs states of bounde…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that high-temperature fermionic Gibbs states are convex combinations of Gaussian states, enabling efficient classical simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems at finite temperature is challenging; structural properties like Gaussianity can enable efficient algorithms.
method: The authors use cluster expansion and combinatorial arguments to show that the Gibbs state of a bounded-degree fermionic Hamiltonian at sufficiently high temperature can be expressed as a mixture of Gaussian states.
result: They establish a rigorous bound on the temperature above which the Gibbs state is a mixture of Gaussian states, and demonstrate that this implies efficient classical simulation via Monte Carlo methods.
conclusion: The work provides a new structural insight into high-temperature fermionic systems, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Improving Shadow Estimation With Locally Optimal Dual Frames
authors: Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, And Daniel Cavalcanti
abstract:
Author(s): Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, and Daniel Cavalcanti

Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is a central challenge in quantum information science, yet practical implementations are fundamentally constrained by the limited number of measurement shots. In this work, we explore a variation of the classical shadows protocol in which the mea…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012428] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves classical shadow estimation by using locally optimal dual frames to reduce the number of measurement shots needed for accurate observable estimation.
motivation: Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is limited by the number of measurement shots; classical shadows offer a scalable approach but can be inefficient for certain observables.
method: The authors propose a variation of the classical shadows protocol where the measurement basis is chosen adaptively using locally optimal dual frames, optimizing the estimation variance.
result: The locally optimal dual frames reduce the required number of shots compared to standard classical shadows, especially for observables with low-rank structure.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement to shadow estimation, making it more efficient for near-term quantum devices.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that aims to characterize quantum correlations, but existing formulations leave gaps for certain families of correlations.
method: The authors introduce a new quantifier for information causality based on a more general communication task, going beyond the standard random-access-code model.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the gaps, providing tighter bounds on the set of quantum correlations.
conclusion: Information causality remains a powerful principle for understanding quantum nonlocality, and the proposed generalization improves its predictive power.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in capturing both populations and coherences in open quantum systems.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; the authors aim to systematically understand and quantify these limitations using optimization techniques.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a semidefinite program (SDP) to find the best possible Lindblad equation that approximates a given exact dynamics, and analyze the constraints on populations and coherences.
result: They derive rigorous bounds on the accuracy of Lindblad descriptions, showing that certain features of the exact dynamics cannot be captured by any Markovian master equation.
conclusion: The work provides a clear, quantitative understanding of when Lindblad equations are insufficient, guiding the development of more accurate non-Markovian approaches.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:

method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the driven many-body system and quantify the computational advantage through entanglement measures and sampling complexity.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is both verifiable and relevant for simulating many-body physics, with clear evidence of entanglement generation beyond classical simulability.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform provides a viable path to practical quantum advantage in simulating many-body systems, advancing the field of quantum information processing.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the uncorrected one.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security

abstract:

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced discrete modulation (e.g., QPSK) with a security analysis using the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization to prove composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 100 km with composable security, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: This work makes high-speed, secure quantum key distribution more practical, bringing quantum networks closer to real-world deployment.

tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars

tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in quantum many-body systems, particularly those arising from long-range interactions and kinetic constraints, is a key challenge. Cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays provide a tunable platform to explore such phenomena.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between cavity-mediated long-range interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They discover two distinct regimes: blockaded ferromagnetism, where the cavity suppresses superradiance, and long-range quantum scars, which are non-thermal eigenstates with persistent oscillations.
conclusion: The work establishes cavity-QED with Rydberg arrays as a versatile platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and non-equilibrium phases, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and employ computer algebra to systematically optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum state transfer and gate operations compared to standard variational approaches.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme leads to a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression via erasure conversion, enhancing the viability of superconducting qubits for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, providing a unified framework for symmetry learning.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that would detect entanglement between two quantum probes mediated by gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity using current or near-future technology.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with GIE experiments offering a promising avenue.

title: A Complexity Theory For Non-local Quantum Computation
authors: Andreas Bluhm, Simon Höfer, Alex May, Mikka Stasiuk, Philip Verduyn Lunel, And Henry Yuen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2152 (2026).

Non-local quantum computation (NLQC) replaces a local interaction between two systems with a single round of communication and shared entanglement. Despite many partial results, it is known that a characterization of entanglement cost in at least certain NLQC tasks would imply significant breakthroughs in complexity theory. Here, we avoid these obstructions and take an indirect approach to understanding resource requirements in NLQC, which mimics the approach used by complexity theorists: we study the relative hardness of different NLQC tasks by identifying resource efficient reductions between them. Most significantly, we prove that [MATH]-measure and [MATH]-route, the two best studied NLQC tasks, are in fact equivalent under [MATH] overhead reductions. This result simplifies many existing proofs in the literature and extends several new properties to [MATH]-measure. For instance, we obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on [MATH]-measure for all functions, and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class [MATH]. Beyond this, we study a number of other examples of NLQC tasks and their relationships.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complexity-theoretic framework for non-local quantum computation, showing equivalence between two key tasks and providing efficient protocols for functions in certain complexity classes.
motivation: Characterizing the entanglement cost of non-local quantum computation (NLQC) is known to be difficult and related to major complexity theory problems. The authors aim to circumvent these obstructions by studying relative hardness of NLQC tasks via resource-efficient reductions.
method: The authors introduce reductions between NLQC tasks, analogous to complexity theory reductions, and prove that the two best-studied tasks, f-measure and f-route, are equivalent under polynomial overhead reductions. They also analyze other NLQC tasks and their relationships.
result: They prove that f-measure and f-route are equivalent under polynomial overhead reductions, obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on f-measure for all functions, and provide efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class P.
conclusion: The work simplifies existing proofs, extends properties to f-measure, and establishes a complexity-theoretic approach to NLQC that may lead to further insights into the resource requirements of non-local quantum computation.

title: Learning Thermodynamic Master Equations For Open Quantum Systems
authors: Peter Sentz, Stanley Nicholson, Yujin Cho, Sohail Reddy, Brendan Keith, And Stefanie Günther
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2151 (2026).

The characterization of Hamiltonians and other components of open quantum dynamical systems plays a crucial role in quantum computing and other applications. Scientific machine learning techniques have been applied to this problem in a variety of ways, including by modeling with deep neural networks. However, the majority of mathematical models describing open quantum systems are linear, and the natural nonlinearities in learnable models have not been incorporated using physical principles. We present a data-driven model for open quantum systems that includes learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms. The trained model is interpretable, as it directly estimates the system Hamiltonian and linear components of coupling to the environment. We validate the model on synthetic two and three-level data, as well as experimental two-level data collected from a quantum device at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

.
tldr: A data-driven model for open quantum systems that learns thermodynamically consistent master equations from data.
motivation: Characterizing Hamiltonians and dissipative dynamics of open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing, but existing machine learning approaches often lack thermodynamic consistency.
method: The authors propose a neural network model that incorporates learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms, directly estimating the system Hamiltonian and linear coupling to the environment.
result: The model is validated on synthetic two- and three-level data and experimental two-level data from a quantum device, demonstrating accurate and interpretable recovery of system parameters.
conclusion: The approach provides a physically principled, interpretable machine learning framework for learning open quantum system dynamics, with potential applications in quantum device characterization and control.

title: Multi-product Zeno Effect Achieving Higher Order Convergence Rates
authors: Tim Möbus
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2148 (2026).

The quantum Zeno effect is a fundamental mechanism for implementing the effective dynamics of projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian systems. It approximates the target projected evolution by interleaving Hamiltonian or Lindblad dynamics with quantum operations associated with the desired subspace. In contrast to the related Trotter product formula, the best-known convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect is typically limited to order [MATH]. In this work, we improve this convergence rate by employing a multi-product formula, thereby achieving arbitrarily high-order convergence of the form [MATH]. This yields an improved approximation scheme for Zeno-like expectation values via an efficient post-processing method. The approach combines a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation. We illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and also consider the broader class of systems governed by the Bang-Bang decoupling method.

.
tldr: This paper improves the convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect to arbitrarily high order using a multi-product formula, with applications to projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian dynamics.
motivation: The standard quantum Zeno effect has a limited convergence rate (order 1), which restricts its efficiency in approximating projected dynamics. Achieving higher-order convergence would enable more accurate simulations and control.
method: The authors combine a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation to construct a multi-product formula that yields arbitrarily high-order convergence.
result: They prove that the multi-product Zeno effect achieves convergence of order k for any integer k, and demonstrate the method on the bosonic cat code and Bang-Bang decoupling.
conclusion: The multi-product Zeno effect provides a systematic way to enhance the accuracy of Zeno-based approximations, with potential applications in quantum control and simulation.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control over a quantum system manipulates its environment, enabling new functionalities in open quantum systems.
motivation: Standard quantum reservoir engineering uses structured environments as entropy sinks, but active control over the system can reverse this role, allowing the system to act as an entropy sink for the environment.
method: The authors develop a framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrate it with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: The framework qualitatively reproduces previous experimental results and shows how active control can unlock new functionalities, such as manipulating the environment via repeated initialization of the quantum system.
conclusion: Active reservoir engineering provides a versatile tool for controlling open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes that encode the combinatorial Laplacian, enabling superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: Quantum walks on graphs have shown advantages, but extending them to simplicial complexes could unlock new quantum algorithms for topological data analysis and homology computation.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by operating on a doubled state space of oriented simplices, using coherent interference to project onto harmonic cycles.
result: They achieve an apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying a QMA-hard problem, and solving the high-dimensional Dirichlet problem, without quantum oracles.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide significant quantum advantages in topological data analysis and related areas, opening new avenues for quantum algorithms.

title: Exploring Variational Entanglement Hamiltonians
authors: Yanick S. Kind And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2133 (2026).

Recent advances in analog and digital quantum-simulation platforms have enabled exploration of the spectrum of entanglement Hamiltonians via variational algorithms. In this work we analyze the convergence properties of the variationally obtained solutions and compare them to numerically exact calculations in quantum critical systems. We demonstrate that interpreting the cost functional as an integral permits the deployment of iterative quadrature schemes, thereby reducing the required number of measurements by more than an order of magnitude even in the presence of noise. We further show that a modified ansatz captures deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models, improves convergence, improves trainability and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Finally, we establish that a low cost value does not by itself guarantee convergence in trace distance. Nevertheless, it faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps, which are essential for applications to topological phases.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes variational entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum critical systems, demonstrating improved convergence and measurement efficiency.
motivation: Understanding entanglement Hamiltonians is crucial for characterizing quantum many-body systems, but their experimental extraction is challenging. Variational methods offer a practical approach, yet their convergence properties and reliability need systematic study.
method: The authors interpret the cost functional as an integral, enabling iterative quadrature schemes to reduce measurements. They also introduce a modified ansatz to capture deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models.
result: The iterative quadrature reduces required measurements by over an order of magnitude even with noise. The modified ansatz improves convergence and trainability, and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Low cost value does not guarantee convergence in trace distance but faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps.
conclusion: Variational entanglement Hamiltonians can be efficiently optimized and provide reliable spectral information, making them a useful tool for studying topological phases and quantum criticality.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends to a family of codes for higher-order damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common error in quantum systems, and existing codes are not optimized for this noise model. The authors aim to construct small, efficient codes tailored to amplitude damping.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code using a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery, and generalize it to a family of codes that correct up to any fixed order in damping strength. They also derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes corrects errors up to arbitrary order. The noise-adapted Hamming bound provides a fundamental limit for such codes.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that small, efficient quantum error-correcting codes can be designed for specific noise models, with potential applications in quantum memory and communication.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics, which are computationally expensive, using a photonic platform that is highly configurable.
method: Decomposes a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: Demonstrates a configurable photonic simulator that can execute quantum field dynamics simulations with high efficiency.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical and scalable approach to studying quantum field dynamics.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's Wigner function negativity and other non-Gaussianity measures.
result: The symplectic rank provides an operational interpretation as the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations required for state preparation, and it also bounds the compression rate and measurement complexity.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a fundamental resource measure for non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

tldr: This paper demonstrates a scalable method to manipulate large quantum states by mapping Fock-space representations to classical wave propagation, using superconducting circuits.

method: The authors experimentally realize a mapping from Fock-space eigenstates to classical wave propagation in a superconducting circuit, enabling control of large bosonic quantum states.

title: Hybrid Nanophotonic Trap For Cold Atoms Using Surface Forces And A Blue-detuned Evanescent Field
authors: Riccardo Pennetta

tldr: A hybrid nanophotonic trap for cold atoms using surface forces and blue-detuned evanescent field achieves efficient loading and enhanced storage and coherence times.
motivation: To improve the performance of atom-based quantum devices by combining nanophotonics with cold atoms, addressing challenges in loading efficiency and coherence.
method: The trap uses surface forces (Casimir-Polder) for attraction and a blue-detuned evanescent field for repulsion, creating a stable potential for cold caesium atoms near a nanophotonic waveguide.
result: Demonstrated efficient loading, long storage times, and enhanced coherence times compared to previous traps.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers a promising platform for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems, integrating cold atoms with nanophotonic circuits.

title: Exponential Linewidth Narrowing And Enhancement Of Sensitivity In Ramsey Interferometry With An Optically Thick Ensemble Of Atoms
authors: S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, And E. S. Moiseev
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, and E. S. Moiseev

Ramsey resonance is a high-resolution technique used in spectroscopy, precise measurement of time and frequency, and the creation of modern clocks. The Ramsey experiments are typically done in optically dilute samples of atoms to improve homogeneity and avoid backaction of atoms on excitation pulses…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates exponential narrowing of Ramsey resonance linewidth and enhanced sensitivity using an optically thick atomic ensemble, enabled by collective effects and coherent control.
motivation: Ramsey interferometry is limited by inhomogeneous broadening and optical thickness; the authors aim to overcome these limitations using collective effects in dense ensembles.
method: They theoretically and experimentally study Ramsey interferometry in an optically thick ensemble of rare-earth ions, exploiting collective dipole-dipole interactions and a specific pulse sequence to suppress inhomogeneous broadening.
result: They observe an exponential narrowing of the Ramsey fringe linewidth and a corresponding increase in sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach to high-precision spectroscopy and quantum sensing using dense atomic ensembles, with potential applications in quantum memories and networks.

title: How Lorentz Boosts Reshape Relaxation Spectra
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

In relativity, relaxation processes are often assumed to undergo time dilation under Lorentz boosts. We show that this intuition fails generically. Because of relativity of simultaneity, Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, with a width set by the maxima…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, challenging the naive expectation of time dilation in relativistic relaxation processes.
motivation: Understanding how relaxation processes behave under Lorentz boosts is crucial for relativistic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The author analyzes the effect of Lorentz boosts on relaxation spectra using relativistic kinetic theory and the concept of relativity of simultaneity.
result: A single relaxation mode is shown to broaden into a continuum of excitations with a width set by the maximum boost factor, contradicting simple time dilation.
conclusion: Relaxation spectra are not invariant under boosts, which has implications for relativistic fluid dynamics and the formulation of thermodynamics in moving frames.

title: Path Integral Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Hilbert Kappen
abstract:
Author(s): Aarón Villanueva and Hilbert Kappen

We investigate open-loop quantum state preparation for a class of open quantum systems whose dynamics follow a Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation that admits a trajectory-based stochastic representation. The deterministic control objective is reformulated as a stochastic op…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012426] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path integral control framework for open quantum systems described by GKLS master equations, enabling efficient open-loop state preparation.
motivation: Controlling open quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but optimal control is computationally challenging due to the high-dimensional nature of the density matrix.
method: The authors reformulate the deterministic control objective as a stochastic optimal control problem using a trajectory-based representation of the GKLS master equation, then apply path integral control theory to derive an analytical solution.
result: They demonstrate that the optimal control can be expressed as an expectation over stochastic trajectories, which can be efficiently computed via Monte Carlo sampling, avoiding the curse of dimensionality.
conclusion: The path integral approach provides a scalable method for open-loop control of open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum state preparation and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Modeling Dissipation In Quantum Active Matter
authors: Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, And Michael Te Vrugt
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, and Michael te Vrugt

Active matter is characterized by a constant influx and dissipation of energy that gives rise to directed motion. Dissipation requires interactions with an external environment, such that extending the paradigm of active matter to a quantum framework requires an appropriate description of this envir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for modeling dissipation in quantum active matter, bridging quantum thermodynamics and active matter physics.
motivation: Active matter systems require constant energy dissipation, and extending this to quantum regimes necessitates a proper description of the environment and dissipation mechanisms.
method: The authors derive a quantum master equation for active particles by coupling them to a thermal bath and incorporating non-equilibrium driving, using techniques from open quantum systems and stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They obtain a general framework that captures the interplay between quantum coherence, dissipation, and directed motion, and illustrate it with specific examples.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for studying quantum active matter from a thermodynamic perspective, highlighting the role of information and entropy production.

title: Emergence Of Nonequilibrium Latent Cycles In Unsupervised Generative Modeling
authors: Marco Baiesi And Alberto Rosso
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baiesi and Alberto Rosso

The authors provide a nonequilibrium perspective on generative modeling in machine learning, complementing recent efforts to accelerate sampling in energy-based models and to analyze diffusion models through thermodynamic principles. They show that breaking detailed balance, rather than merely correcting for slow equilibrium mixing, can yield qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics.

#MachineLearningSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies nonequilibrium thermodynamics to generative modeling, showing that breaking detailed balance improves learning dynamics.
motivation: To understand and improve generative models through thermodynamic principles, specifically by analyzing the role of nonequilibrium latent cycles.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework connecting nonequilibrium thermodynamics with unsupervised generative modeling, focusing on breaking detailed balance in latent dynamics.
result: Breaking detailed balance yields qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics, accelerating sampling and improving model performance.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics provides a useful perspective for designing and analyzing generative models, with practical benefits for machine learning.

title: Nonanaliticities And Ergodicity Breaking In Noninteracting Many-body Dynamics Via Stochastic Resetting And Global Measurements
authors: David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Stochastic resetting generates nonequilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary quantum dynamics with resets at random times. When the state to which the system is reset is chosen conditionally on the outcome of a global and spatially resolved measurement, the steady state can feature collectiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014105] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking in noninteracting many-body dynamics under stochastic resetting and global measurements.
motivation: Understanding how stochastic resetting and measurements can induce nonequilibrium steady states with collective behavior and ergodicity breaking is of fundamental interest in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a noninteracting many-body system subject to stochastic resetting to a state conditioned on a global measurement outcome, using analytical and numerical methods to study the steady-state properties.
result: They find that the steady state exhibits nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking, characterized by a phase transition in the resetting rate.
conclusion: The work reveals that even noninteracting systems can display complex nonequilibrium phenomena when combined with resetting and measurements, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Anharmonic Motion Of A Trapped Ion Under The Influence Of Different Drives In An Ion-nanomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Adrien Poindron And Stefan Willitsch
abstract:
Author(s): Adrien Poindron and Stefan Willitsch

Ions in traps hybridized with nanomechanical oscillators represent promising platforms for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating the classical and quantum motion of trapped particles. In a previous report [Weegen et al.,
tldr: This paper studies the anharmonic motion of a trapped ion coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator under various drives, analyzing classical and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Hybrid ion-nanomechanical systems are promising for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating trapped particle motion.
method: The authors model the system using a Hamiltonian that includes anharmonic trapping potentials and different drive schemes, solving the equations of motion analytically and numerically.
result: They characterize the anharmonic motion and its dependence on drive parameters, showing how nonlinearities affect the dynamics and can be controlled.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling trapped ion motion in hybrid systems, relevant for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, including squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are crucial for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: Using a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states via laser pulses, the authors implement a protocol to create superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating control over quantum harmonic oscillator states beyond Gaussian operations.
conclusion: This work advances the capability to engineer complex quantum states in trapped ions, with direct applications to quantum sensing and error correction.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The demonstrated techniques enable new capabilities for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally study a nonlinear coupling (cosφ) and perform numerical simulations to analyze the complex dynamics that suppress these transitions.
result: They demonstrate that the nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, enabling higher-fidelity readout.
conclusion: The proposed coupling scheme offers a practical path to improving transmon readout fidelity, which is important for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Trapped ions offer a clean platform, but achieving optimal sensitivity requires engineering non-classical states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by coupling the ion's internal spin to its motional state via a spin-dependent force, then perform a displacement measurement.
result: They achieve displacement sensitivity at the Heisenberg limit, demonstrating optimal sensing with spin-dependent squeezed states.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
