motivation: Fracton quantum spin liquids described by higher-rank gauge theories have been elusive in microscopic spin models; this work aims to demonstrate such a phase in a simple spin-1 square lattice model.
method: The authors perform Green function Monte Carlo simulations on a spin-1 square lattice model to compute spin structure factors and identify signatures of a rank-2 U(1) fracton quantum spin liquid.
result: They observe suppressed pinch points and emergent photon-like excitations, consistent with a gapless fracton quantum spin liquid.
conclusion: The work provides evidence for a fracton quantum spin liquid in a microscopic model, but the connection to quantum information theory is indirect and not a core focus.

title: Chip-integrated Metasurface-enabled Single-photon Skyrmion Sources
authors: Xujing Liu

motivation: Single-photon skyrmions are challenging to generate due to nanoscale confinement of quantum emitters; the work aims to achieve room-temperature, magnetic-field-free on-chip generation.
method: A metasurface is integrated with a quantum emitter (likely a color center) to structure the emitted photon's polarization and phase, creating skyrmionic states.
result: Room-temperature on-chip generation of single-photon skyrmions is demonstrated without external magnetic fields.
conclusion: The platform enables compact sources of structured single photons, which may be useful for quantum information and communication applications.

title: Resource-efficient Simulations Of Particle Scattering On A Digital Quantum Computer
authors: Yahui Chai

motivation: Particle scattering simulations are important for high-energy physics but require significant quantum resources; the authors aim to reduce the cost.
method: They use a combination of variational quantum algorithms and error mitigation techniques to simulate scattering processes with fewer qubits and gates.
result: The proposed methods achieve accurate scattering amplitudes with reduced resource requirements compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Resource-efficient quantum simulations of scattering are feasible on near-term quantum devices, advancing practical applications in quantum field theory.

title: Skeleton Of Isometric Tensor Network States For Abelian String-Net Models
authors: Julian Boesl, Yu-Jie Liu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:

We construct parametrized isometric tensor network states—referred to as “skeletons”—that allow us to explore phases of Abelian topological order and can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors. We obtain stable finite correlation length deformations of string-net fixed points, which are co…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs parametrized isometric tensor network states for Abelian string-net models, enabling efficient exploration of topological phases on quantum processors.
motivation: String-net models describe topological phases of matter, but their fixed-point states are difficult to deform while preserving topological order. The authors aim to create stable finite correlation length deformations that can be implemented on quantum hardware.
method: The authors develop 'skeleton' isometric tensor network states that parametrize deformations of string-net fixed points, using isometric constraints to ensure stability and efficient representation.
result: They obtain stable finite correlation length deformations of Abelian string-net fixed points, and show that these states can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors.
conclusion: The skeleton approach provides a practical way to study topological phases and their deformations using tensor networks and quantum simulation.

result: Measured hyperfine structure of 7p, 7s, and 6d states and second-order Zeeman coefficient of the ground state.

title: Physics-inspired Transformer Quantum States Via Latent Imaginary-time Evolution
authors: Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, And Yoshinobu Kawahara
abstract:

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. tldr: This paper proposes a physically transparent framework for neural quantum states by interpreting them as approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution, improving accuracy and efficiency for ground state calculations.
motivation: Neural quantum states are powerful but often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated architecture that improves performance and interpretability.
method: The authors introduce a framework where neural quantum states are viewed as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution, and they design a transformer-based architecture that incorporates this physical prior.
result: The proposed method achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence compared to standard neural quantum state approaches on benchmark spin systems.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that incorporating physical principles into neural network architectures can significantly enhance variational Monte Carlo calculations for quantum many-body systems.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing quasiparticle excitations in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: Demonstrates the algorithm on a spin model, showing accurate excitation energies with modest quantum resources.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach is feasible for near-term quantum devices and extends NLCE to quantum computing.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard, and belief propagation provides an approximate method but lacks systematic error control.
method: The authors propose cluster corrections to belief propagation, which incorporate local correlations beyond the tree approximation, and prove exponential convergence of the approximation error.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial-time contraction with rigorous error bounds, outperforming standard belief propagation on several benchmarks.
conclusion: Cluster-corrected belief propagation offers a practical and provably accurate approach for tensor network contraction, relevant to quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires high overhead; the authors aim to reduce both qubit and time overhead using advanced quantum LDPC codes.
method: The scheme employs parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques enabled by good quantum LDPC codes.
result: The approach achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making it more practical.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi

result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological effects.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.

method: The authors design and implement a quantum algorithm that combines state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement to estimate the Jones polynomial, and run it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and demonstrating the algorithm's feasibility on current hardware.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial approximation as a practical benchmark for quantum computers, but it is primarily a demonstration of quantum advantage in a computational complexity context rather than advancing quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of a unified approach based on space-time duality.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and focuses on brickwork quantum circuits as a framework.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems through the lens of quantum computation and space-time duality.
conclusion: The space-time duality approach offers a powerful tool for understanding and computing quantum dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

title: When Nearby Materials Steal Energy
authors: R. A. Norte
G. J. Verbiest
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies energy loss in high-quality mechanical resonators due to nearby dielectric materials, focusing on charge fluctuations.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating energy loss is crucial for improving the performance of mechanical resonators in devices.
method: Systematic experimental study of dielectric environments to measure energy loss in mechanical resonators.
result: Dielectric materials cause energy loss through charge fluctuations, which can be significant when resonators are brought close to them.
conclusion: Careful selection and placement of materials are necessary to minimize energy loss in high-quality mechanical resonators.

title: Visualization Of The Zhang–Rice Singlet, Electronic Molecules And Cooper Pair Formation In A Cuprate Superconductor
authors: Shusen Ye
Jianfa Zhao
Zhiheng Yao
Sixuan Chen
Runze Yu
Zehao Dong
Zhenqi Hao
Xintong Li
Luchuan Shi
Qingqing Liu
Changqing Jin
Yayu Wang
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: This paper visualizes the Zhang-Rice singlet, electronic molecules, and Cooper pair formation in a cuprate superconductor using scanning tunneling microscopy.
motivation: The mechanism of Cooper pair formation in high-temperature superconductors remains poorly understood. Direct observation of the evolution from individual doped holes to Cooper pairs could provide crucial insights.
method: The authors used scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to image the electronic structure of a cuprate superconductor at different doping levels, tracking the formation of Zhang-Rice singlets and their pairing into Cooper pairs.
result: They observed the transition from isolated Zhang-Rice singlets to electronic molecules and finally to Cooper pairs as doping increased, providing direct visualization of the pairing process.
conclusion: The study offers a microscopic picture of Cooper pair formation in cuprates, supporting the role of magnetic interactions in pairing.

title: Electro-optic Comb-empowered Measurement Of The Dynamic Frequency Of A Laser
authors: Weiwei Yang
Xingyu Jia
Jingyi Wang
Xinlun Cai
Yang Li
Guanhao Wu
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method for measuring the dynamic frequency of a laser using electro-optic frequency combs on an integrated lithium niobate platform, applied to high-precision 3D ranging.
motivation: Accurate measurement of laser frequency variations is crucial for applications like LiDAR and spectroscopy; existing methods are limited in speed or precision.
method: Two electro-optic frequency combs with slightly different repetition rates are generated on a lithium niobate chip; the beat note between them tracks the frequency modulation of a laser.
result: The technique enables stable and high-precision 3D scene ranging, demonstrating the utility of integrated photonic combs for dynamic frequency metrology.
conclusion: Integrated lithium niobate electro-optic combs provide a compact, high-performance solution for laser frequency tracking and ranging applications.

abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates lightwave-driven scanning tunnelling microscopy with attosecond time resolution to observe individual electrons during tunnelling.
motivation: Understanding electron tunnelling dynamics at the fastest timescales is fundamental to quantum physics and could enable ultrafast electronics.
method: The authors combine scanning tunnelling microscopy with attosecond laser pulses to achieve simultaneous spatial and temporal resolution of tunnelling electrons.
result: They successfully track individual electrons as they tunnel through an energy barrier, capturing the process in real time.
conclusion: This technique opens the door to observing quantum phenomena at the space-time limit, with potential applications in ultrafast science and quantum control.

title: Harnessing Loss For Q-modulated Biosensors
authors: Yohan Lee
Andreas Tittl
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a nanophotonic biosensing strategy using radiative Q-factor modulation in a BIC metasurface for ultrasensitive detection of tumor extracellular vesicles.
motivation: To achieve ultrasensitive and rapid biosensing of low-concentration biomarkers such as tumor extracellular vesicles.
method: The authors design a bound-state-in-the-continuum (BIC) metasurface that converts refractive-index changes into large intensity variations via radiative Q-factor modulation.
result: The sensor detects a few tens of tumor extracellular vesicles within 15 minutes, demonstrating high sensitivity and scalability.
conclusion: The proposed Q-modulated biosensing strategy offers a promising platform for rapid, label-free, and scalable biosensing applications.

title: Non-idealities In Artificial Synapses
authors: Shafin Bin Hamid
Jean Anne C. Incorvia
Samuel Liu
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews non-idealities in artificial synapses based on non-volatile memory for neuromorphic computing.
motivation: Non-ideal effects in artificial synapses can limit neuromorphic system performance, so understanding their origins and mitigation is important.
method: The paper reviews various non-idealities, their physical origins, and discusses mitigation strategies and opportunities to exploit them.
result: It categorizes non-idealities and presents strategies to mitigate or exploit them for new computing functionalities.
conclusion: Non-idealities in artificial synapses are both challenges and opportunities for neuromorphic computing.

tldr: This paper reviews terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy for ultrafast electron dynamics, but does not align with the specified research directions.
motivation: To achieve ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution for studying ultrafast phenomena in quantum materials.
method: Integrates picosecond terahertz pulses with scanning tunnelling microscopy.
result: Enables detailed analysis of electron dynamics and molecular motions at atomic resolution.
conclusion: The technique offers insights into ultrafast phenomena and potential advances in quantum materials and technologies.

authors: A. Jadbabaie

motivation: To explore new physics at energy scales beyond colliders using molecular quantum control and precision measurements.
method: Review of advances in production, trapping, and quantum control of radioactive molecules.
result: Radioactive molecules offer a promising platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations.
conclusion: These molecules can complement high-energy collider searches for new physics.

authors: Yihan Wang, Domenico Bongiovanni, Dario Jukić, Sihong Lei, Zhichan Hu, Daohong Song, Jingjun Xu, Roberto Morandotti, Hrvoje Buljan, And Zhigang Chen

motivation: To understand how angular momentum conservation is modified in discrete lattices due to nontrivial momentum-space band touchings.
method: Theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration using photonic lattices with quadratic band touching and nontrivial winding.
result: They reveal generalized angular momentum conservation laws arising from the band structure topology.
conclusion: The work provides insight into angular momentum in discrete systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper studies anyon bound states and hybrid superconductivity in the context of fractional quantum Hall effect, using Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory.
motivation: To understand the interactions of anyonic quasiparticles and their relation to superconductivity types.
method: Theoretical analysis within Chern-Simons-Landau-Ginzburg theory, examining vortex interactions and Gauss's law.
result: The system realizes a hybridization of type I and type II superconductivity.
conclusion: Anyon bound states in fractional quantum Hall systems exhibit hybrid superconducting behavior.

authors: Xiao-Han Yang, Ji-Yao Chen, And Xiao-Yu Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Han Yang, Ji-Yao Chen, and Xiao-Yu Dong

Edge excitations are the defining signature of chiral topologically ordered systems. In continuum fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, these excitations are described by the chiral Luttinger liquid ([MATH]) theory. Whether these field theory predictions can be precisely identified in discre…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026504] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral edge excitations of fractional Chern insulators in the bosonic Hofstadter model, focusing on topological order in lattice systems.
motivation: To verify whether chiral Luttinger liquid theory predictions for fractional quantum Hall edge excitations hold in discrete lattice models of fractional Chern insulators.
method: Numerical simulations using exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) to compute edge spectra and entanglement properties.
result: They identify chiral edge excitations consistent with the predicted Luttinger liquid theory, confirming the topological nature of the fractional Chern insulator phase.
conclusion: The bosonic Hofstadter model at filling ν=1/2 hosts a fractional Chern insulator with chiral edge modes described by the same field theory as fractional quantum Hall states.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Regge trajectories in matrix quantum mechanics, connecting to string theory in AdS, but does not align with the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand the large N limit of matrix quantum mechanics and its critical behavior near a potential maximum, which relates to string theory in AdS.
method: Reexamines the large N limit of O(N) symmetric quantum mechanics of a Hermitian matrix, using the singlet sector solved by free fermions.
result: Finds critical behavior corresponding to string theory in AdS when the Fermi level approaches a maximum of the potential.

title: Unified First-Principles Formula For Time-Resolved Arpes Spectra Of Coherent And Incoherent Excitons Beyond The Dilute Limit
authors: Gianluca Stefanucci And Enrico Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): Gianluca Stefanucci and Enrico Perfetto

Despite major experimental progresses in time-resolved and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, a quantitative, microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced modifications of electronic band structures—applicable even beyond the low-density limit—is still lacking. Here, we close this …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026402] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a first-principles formula for time-resolved ARPES spectra of excitons beyond the dilute limit.
motivation: A quantitative microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced band structure modifications in time-resolved ARPES is lacking, especially beyond the low-density limit.
method: The authors derive a unified formula based on many-body perturbation theory, incorporating both coherent and incoherent exciton contributions.
result: The formula captures excitonic effects in photoemission spectra and is applicable beyond the dilute limit, enabling analysis of high-density exciton systems.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical tool for interpreting time-resolved ARPES experiments on excitonic materials, bridging a gap between theory and experiment.

title: Decoupled-Subspace-Induced Flat Bands In A Photonic Superlattice
authors: Guoxia Yang, Jiayi Zhang, Siyan Jiang, Anwen Jiang, Chenying Huang, Yihe Li, Haojie Li, Xiaoran Zhang, Dahe Liu, And Jinwei Shi
abstract:

Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, yet realizing flat dispersion across an entire Brillouin zone (BZ) remains nontrivial. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026902] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.

motivation: Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, but achieving flat dispersion across the entire Brillouin zone is challenging.
method: The authors design a photonic superlattice where coupling between specific modes leads to decoupled subspaces, resulting in flat bands.
result: They demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that the proposed structure yields flat bands spanning the entire Brillouin zone.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to realizing broadband flat bands in photonic systems, with potential applications in light confinement and nonlinear optics.

title: Spontaneous Quantum Turbulence In A Newborn Bose-Einstein Condensate Via The Kibble-Zurek Mechanism
authors: Seong-Ho Shinn, Matteo Massaro, Mithun Thudiyangal, And Adolfo Del Campo

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating spontaneous quantum turbulence in a Bose-Einstein condensate via the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
motivation: To explore the formation of topological defects and quantum turbulence during a rapid phase transition in a Bose-Einstein condensate.
method: Numerical simulations of a thermal quench in a Bose-Einstein condensate, analyzing defect formation and turbulence.
result: Spontaneous quantum turbulence is observed as a result of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism can generate quantum turbulence in Bose-Einstein condensates, providing a new platform for studying turbulence.

title: Maximum Entropy Conjecture For Black Hole Mergers
authors: Monica Rincon-Ramirez, Nathan K. Johnson-Mcdaniel, Eugenio Bianchi, Ish Gupta, Vaishak Prasad, And B. S. Sathyaprakash
abstract:
Author(s): Monica Rincon-Ramirez, Nathan K. Johnson-McDaniel, Eugenio Bianchi, Ish Gupta, Vaishak Prasad, and B. S. Sathyaprakash

The remnant properties of black hole mergers may be governed by a maximum entropy bound suggesting that once the black holes become sufficiently close together, the throat around both black holes resembles that of an individual Kerr black hole to a far-away observer, and thus the Kerr entropy computation becomes valid.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021406] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a maximum entropy conjecture for black hole mergers, suggesting that the merged remnant's entropy is bounded by that of a Kerr black hole.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties of black hole mergers and whether a maximum entropy principle governs the final state.
method: The authors analyze black hole merger simulations and compare the entropy of the remnant to the Kerr black hole entropy bound.
result: They find evidence supporting the conjecture that the merged black hole's entropy approaches the Kerr bound.
conclusion: The maximum entropy conjecture may provide a thermodynamic constraint on black hole merger outcomes.

motivation: To explore exotic nonequilibrium topological phenomena beyond static systems using Floquet engineering.
method: The authors use a photonic platform with periodic driving to create and braid complex-energy bands, and detect them via single-photon interferometry.
result: They observe braiding of complex-energy bands and confirm topological features in the Floquet system.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new regime of topological physics in non-Hermitian Floquet systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

However, conventional approaches to masers fail to produce emission with embedded OAM. The recent emerg…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates microwave lasing with orbital angular momentum using photonic time crystals.
motivation: Conventional masers cannot produce emission with embedded OAM, limiting applications in communications and sensing.
method: The authors propose and analyze a photonic time crystal structure that supports OAM-carrying modes and achieves lasing through parametric amplification.
result: They show that microwave vortex beams can be generated with controlled OAM states and high efficiency.
conclusion: Photonic time crystals provide a new platform for generating vortex beams in the microwave regime, with potential for advanced applications.

title: Superconductivity From Phonon-Mediated Retardation In A Single-Flavor Metal
authors: Yang-Zhi Chou, Jihang Zhu, Jay D. Sau, And Sankar Das Sarma
abstract:

We study phonon-mediated pairings in a single-flavor metal with a tunable Berry curvature. In the absence of Berry curvature, we discover an unexpected possibility: [MATH]-wave superconductivity emerging purely from the retardation effect, while the static Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) approximation …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated superconductivity in a single-flavor metal with Berry curvature, focusing on retardation effects.
motivation: To understand how Berry curvature and retardation affect phonon-mediated pairing and superconductivity.
method: The authors analyze a model of a single-flavor metal with tunable Berry curvature, comparing static BCS approximation with full retardation effects.
result: They find that retardation alone can induce d-wave superconductivity even without Berry curvature, and Berry curvature modifies the pairing symmetry.
conclusion: Retardation effects are crucial for unconventional superconductivity in single-flavor metals, and Berry curvature provides additional tunability.

title: Thermodynamic Evidence For Pressure-Driven Evolution Towards Weak-Coupling Superconductivity In Pb
authors: Rustem Khasanov
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026002] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field in lead, providing evidence for a transition from strong to weak coupling superconductivity.
motivation: The pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field, which gives direct access to condensation energy, has been less studied than that of the transition temperature.
method: Muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements were used to determine the thermodynamic critical field of lead under pressure.
result: The data show a pressure-driven evolution from strong-coupling to weak-coupling superconductivity.
conclusion: The study provides thermodynamic evidence for the coupling strength transition in lead under pressure.

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013509] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controllable temporal reflection and refraction via coupling phase engineering in optical systems.
motivation: Temporal boundary effects offer a new degree of freedom for optical device design, but controllable manipulation of temporal reflection and refraction remains challenging.
method: The authors use coupling phase engineering to abruptly change the properties of an optical medium, inducing temporal boundaries.
result: They achieve controllable temporal reflection and refraction components.
conclusion: The work provides a method to manipulate light in the time domain, potentially enabling new optical devices.

tldr: This paper attempts to generalize spontaneous collapse models to a relativistic framework, addressing the quantum measurement problem.
motivation: Spontaneous collapse models provide a testable solution to the measurement problem, but a fully relativistic extension is still missing.
method: The authors review previous attempts and obstacles, then propose a new approach to formulate a relativistic collapse model.
result: The paper presents a theoretical framework for a relativistic generalization, though it remains incomplete and faces challenges.
conclusion: A full relativistic collapse model is not yet achieved, but the work provides a step toward that goal.

motivation: Laser cooling and trapping of fermionic isotopes with nonzero nuclear spin is challenging due to complex hyperfine structure; achieving this enables new studies in quantum gases and precision measurements.
method: The authors perform hyperfine spectroscopy on 47Ti and 49Ti, identify suitable cooling transitions, and demonstrate magneto-optical trapping using a multi-level rate equation model.
result: Successful trapping of both fermionic isotopes with high atom numbers and low temperatures, and characterization of hyperfine splittings and transition strengths.

abstract:

tldr: This paper introduces a mechanical analogy for spatiotemporal vortex pulses to quantify their orbital angular momentum.
motivation: The proper quantification of transverse orbital angular momentum in spatiotemporal vortex pulses has been debated, and a simplified model is needed to clarify the underlying physics.
method: The authors model STVPs as a loop of noninteracting point particles traveling along ray trajectories, deriving expressions for the OAM from this mechanical analogy.
result: The ray-mechanical model yields a clear interpretation of the transverse OAM and resolves ambiguities in previous definitions.
conclusion: The mechanical analogy provides an intuitive and consistent framework for understanding OAM in spatiotemporal vortex pulses.

motivation: Understanding how next-nearest-neighbor coupling and disorder affect quantum state propagation in waveguide arrays is important for integrated quantum photonics.
method: The authors use an extended tight-binding model to analyze the dispersion and dynamics of squeezed vacuum in waveguide arrays with NNNC and disorder.
result: NNNC reshapes the dispersion, breaks spectral symmetry, and introduces localization effects due to disorder.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling quantum states in photonic lattices, but the work is primarily a photonic platform study without direct connection to the specified research directions.

title: Analysis Of Collision-shift Assessments In Ion-based Clocks

We consider background gas collision shifts in ion-based clocks. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 013104] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes collision shifts in ion-based clocks using classical and quantum descriptions.
motivation: Accurate timekeeping in ion clocks requires understanding systematic shifts due to background gas collisions.
method: The authors model collisions between an ion and a polarizable particle with hard-sphere repulsion, providing both classical and quantum descriptions.
result: Both descriptions yield consistent results, showing that a collision-shift bound is determined by the polarizability and hard-sphere radius.
conclusion: The analysis provides a framework for estimating collision shifts in ion clocks, which is important for improving clock accuracy.

title: Unconventional Quantum Spin Mixing Of Two Spin-1 Atoms Beyond The Single-mode Approximation

tldr: This paper studies unconventional quantum spin mixing of two spin-1 atoms beyond the single-mode approximation using generalized Van Vleck perturbation theory.
motivation: The single-mode approximation is widely used in ultracold spinor gases but may be inaccurate for certain systems; the authors aim to improve ground-state energy calculations.
method: They adopt generalized Van Vleck (GVV) perturbation theory to derive an effective Hamiltonian that goes beyond the single-mode approximation.
result: They achieve a relative error in ground-state energy with a reduced effective Hamiltonian.
conclusion: The GVV perturbation theory provides a more accurate description of spin mixing in two spin-1 atoms, highlighting limitations of the single-mode approximation.

method: The authors use mean-field theory and numerical methods to compute the phase diagram for weakly interacting BECs in various trapping potentials.
result: They find discontinuous transitions between vortex states as rotation frequency varies, with the phase diagram depending on trap shape and interaction strength.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed phase diagram for rotating BECs but does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects relevant to the user's interests.

authors: Jacob L. Barnett And Ramy El-Ganainy

tldr: This paper introduces a framework for realizing PT-like phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems using square roots of supersymmetric Hamiltonians.
motivation: To achieve PT-like phase transitions without requiring explicit PT symmetry, broadening the scope of non-Hermitian physics.
method: Constructs a Hamiltonian as the square root of a supersymmetric partner Hamiltonian shifted by a constant, then analyzes its eigenvalue structure.
result: The framework yields PT-like phase transitions in systems that are not PT-symmetric, demonstrated analytically.
conclusion: This approach provides a new route to study non-Hermitian phase transitions beyond conventional PT symmetry.

title: Classically Tuning The Quantum Interference Of Two Photons Scattered By A Macroscopic Lossy Sphere
authors: A. Ciattoni
abstract:
Author(s): A. Ciattoni

We investigate the quantum optical scattering of two-photon wave packets by a macroscopic lossy sphere by means of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics in the form of modified Langevin noise formalism. Building on our recently developed general scattering framework, we show that under the far-field a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013707] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum interference of two photons scattered by a macroscopic lossy sphere using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: To understand how classical macroscopic objects affect quantum interference of photons, which is fundamental for quantum optics.
method: Uses macroscopic quantum electrodynamics with modified Langevin noise formalism to model two-photon scattering from a lossy sphere.
result: Shows that under far-field conditions, the quantum interference pattern can be tuned by classical parameters of the sphere.
conclusion: Classical macroscopic objects can control quantum interference, but the work is primarily a quantum optics scattering study without direct connection to the specified research directions.

title: Low-temperature Spin Dynamics And Absence Of Magnetic Order In Layered $α\text{−}{\mathrm{RuI}}_{3}$
authors: Hank C. H. Wu, Benjamin M. Huddart, Francis L. Pratt, Danrui Ni, Robert J. Cava, And Stephen J. Blundell
abstract:

Quantum spin liquids are long-sought for their elusive, never-frozen magnetic states. In layered
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014411] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-temperature spin dynamics in α-RuI3, finding no magnetic order and evidence for a quantum spin liquid state.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic states of matter with never-frozen magnetic fluctuations, and α-RuI3 is a candidate material with a honeycomb lattice related to Kitaev materials.
method: Muon spin relaxation measurements were performed down to 50 mK to probe spin dynamics.
result: Spins remain dynamically fluctuating down to 50 mK, with evidence for 2D spin diffusion.
conclusion: α-RuI3 is a promising candidate for hosting a quantum spin liquid state.

title: Ultrafast Dynamics Of Spin-orbit Entangled Excitons And Magnetic Correlations In The Van Der Waals Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$
authors: Sidhanta Sahu, Anupama Chauhan, Poulami Ghosh, Sayan Routh, Ruturaj Puranik, Setti Thirupathaiah, Siddhartha Lal, Shriganesh Prabhu, Chiranjib Mitra, And N. Kamaraju

tldr: This paper studies spin-orbit entangled excitons and magnetic correlations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS3 using ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy.
motivation: To explore unconventional many-body interactions in correlated electron systems via spin-orbit entangled excitons in 2D antiferromagnets.
method: Nondegenerate isotropic and anisotropic pump-probe reflection spectroscopy to probe ultrafast dynamics.
result: Observed ultrafast dynamics of spin-orbit entangled excitons and magnetic correlations.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into many-body interactions in 2D antiferromagnets, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Majorana String Simulation Of Nonequilibrium Dynamics In Two-dimensional Lattice Fermion Systems
authors: Matteo D'anna, Jannes Nys, And Juan Carrasquilla
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo D'Anna, Jannes Nys, and Juan Carrasquilla

Simulating the real-time dynamics of fermionic systems remains a major open problem at the core of understanding materials, chemistry, and other strongly correlated systems. Here, the authors present Majorana propagation, a Heisenberg-picture algorithm that evolves observables in a Majorana-string basis. Benchmarks against tensor network methods and recent quantum experimental data show that the method provides accurate results in the strongly interacting regime in two-dimensional lattices, a notoriously classically hard regime.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034305] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a classical algorithm for simulating nonequilibrium dynamics of fermionic systems using a Majorana-string basis.
motivation: Simulating real-time dynamics of fermionic systems is a major challenge for understanding strongly correlated materials and chemistry.
method: The authors introduce Majorana propagation, a Heisenberg-picture algorithm that evolves observables in a Majorana-string basis.
result: Benchmarks against tensor network methods and quantum experimental data show accurate results in the strongly interacting regime on 2D lattices.
conclusion: The method provides a classical simulation tool for a notoriously hard regime, but does not directly advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Geometry, Localization, And Topological Bounds Of Spin Fluctuations
authors: Carlos Saji And Roberto E. Troncoso
abstract:

We study how topological crystalline defects—dislocations—reshape the real-space quantum geometric tensor and act as tunable sources of quantum geometry. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 034412] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how topological crystalline defects enhance quantum geometry in spin systems, linking lattice topology to Hilbert-space geometry.
motivation: To understand how dislocations in crystalline materials affect the quantum geometric tensor and spin fluctuations.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the real-space quantum geometric tensor in the presence of dislocations, using topological bounds and localization concepts.
result: Dislocations strongly enhance the quantum metric, establishing a direct link between lattice topology and Hilbert-space geometry.
conclusion: Topological defects can serve as tunable sources of quantum geometry, with implications for spin fluctuation phenomena.

title: High-order Angular Hall Response In Multiband Semimetals
authors: Arpan Manna And Soumik Mukhopadhyay
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies high-order angular harmonics in the Hall response of multiband semimetals, focusing on magnetotransport characterization.
motivation: Understanding carrier imbalances in multiband semimetals is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze angular harmonics of magnetotransport and observe a threefold modulation in the Hall response at low temperatures.
result: A robust threefold modulation superimposed on the conventional angular Hall response is observed, characterizing carrier imbalances.
conclusion: The work provides a method to probe carrier imbalances via angular Hall response, but it is purely a condensed matter transport study.

title: Electronic Phonon–induced Magnetism In Moiré Mott-Wigner Crystals
authors: Weide Liang, Xiaoying Du, Na Zhang, And Hongyi Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Weide Liang, Xiaoying Du, Na Zhang, and Hongyi Yu

We show that magnetism in moiré Mott-Wigner crystals can be induced by the collective vibration of electrons around their equilibrium positions (namely, electronic phonons), even without the electron-electron spin interaction. Due to a geometric valley-orbit coupling from the Berry phase effect, the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045412] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetism induced by electronic phonons in moiré Mott-Wigner crystals, focusing on a condensed matter phenomenon without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the origin of magnetism in moiré Mott-Wigner crystals beyond conventional spin interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis incorporating geometric valley-orbit coupling from Berry phase effects and collective electronic vibrations (electronic phonons).
result: Magnetism can arise from electronic phonons even without electron-electron spin interaction.
conclusion: Electronic phonons provide a mechanism for magnetism in moiré systems, relevant to condensed matter physics but not to the specified research directions.

title: Optical Helicity Density In The Thermal Near Field Of Twisted Bilayer Van Der Waals Materials
authors: Xiaohong Zhang, Chiyu Yang, Wenshan Cai, And Zhuomin M. Zhang
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045414] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the optical helicity density in the thermal near field of twisted bilayer van der Waals materials, focusing on phonon polaritons and topological transitions.
motivation: Understanding the thermal near-field properties of twisted bilayer materials is important for nanophotonics and thermal management, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the thermal near field of twisted bilayer van der Waals materials, calculating the optical helicity density and its dependence on twist angle.
result: They find that the optical helicity density can be tuned by the twist angle and exhibits a photonic topological transition at a critical angle.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermal near-field properties of twisted bilayer materials, but has no direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Transmission In A Quantum Wire Manipulated By The non-Hermitian Skin Effect
authors: Cui Jiang, Jia-Rui Li, Jun-Jie Yuan, And Wei-Jiang Gong

Our findings reveal that in this system, the quantum transmission properties are determined by the characteristics of the quantum chain. For the case of the Hermitian c…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045415] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum transmission in a wire coupled to a nonreciprocal chain, focusing on the non-Hermitian skin effect.
motivation: To understand how the non-Hermitian skin effect influences quantum transport in a coupled system.
method: The authors model a quantum wire locally coupled to a nonreciprocal quantum chain and analyze transmission properties using scattering theory.
result: Quantum transmission is determined by the chain's characteristics; the non-Hermitian skin effect can manipulate transmission.
conclusion: The non-Hermitian skin effect provides a mechanism to control quantum transmission in wires.

title: Correlation-driven Phonon Renormalization And The Equation Of State Of $γ$-cerium
authors: Yao Wei, Siyu Chen, Evgeny Plekhanov, Ivan Štich, Cedric Weber, And Jan M. Tomczak
abstract:

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of elemental cerium by assessing the crucial role of phonon free energy within the framework of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). While conventional density functional theory (DFT) often fails to capture the intricate energy landscape of [MATH]-electron mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055110] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamic properties of γ-cerium using DMFT, focusing on phonon renormalization and equation of state.
motivation: Conventional DFT fails to capture the complex energy landscape of f-electron materials like cerium, motivating a more accurate treatment of electronic correlations and lattice dynamics.
method: The authors combine dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) with density functional theory (DFT) to compute electronic structure and phonon free energy, analyzing the equation of state and phonon renormalization.
result: They find that correlation-driven phonon renormalization significantly affects the thermodynamic properties and equation of state of γ-cerium.
conclusion: Including phonon free energy within DMFT is crucial for accurately describing the thermodynamics of strongly correlated materials like cerium.

title: Antihyperbolic Surface Waves With Topological Reconfiguration On Twisted Bilayer Hyperbolic Metasurfaces
authors: Chenxu Bian, Xinyan Zhang, Wenbo Ma, Ao Li, Hongsheng Chen, And Xiao Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxu Bian, Xinyan Zhang, Wenbo Ma, Ao Li, Hongsheng Chen, and Xiao Lin

Twisted bilayer hyperbolic metasurfaces provide versatile control over surface-wave dispersion via rotational stacking, enabling highly directional canalization and flexible wave-front engineering. While prior studies have mainly focused on hyperbolic eigenmodes, the behavior of antihyperbolic surfa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055408] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antihyperbolic surface waves on twisted bilayer hyperbolic metasurfaces, focusing on topological wavefront reconfiguration.
motivation: To explore the behavior of antihyperbolic surface waves, which have been less studied than hyperbolic eigenmodes, and to demonstrate topological reconfiguration of wavefronts via rotational stacking.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and simulate the dispersion and propagation of surface waves on twisted bilayer hyperbolic metasurfaces, using a transfer-matrix method and full-wave simulations.
result: They discover antihyperbolic surface waves that exhibit topological reconfiguration, enabling flexible control of wavefront direction and canalization.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer hyperbolic metasurfaces provide a platform for reconfigurable surface wave control, with potential applications in wavefront engineering and topological photonics.

title: Correlated Phases Of Moat-band Excitons In Two Dimensions
authors: L. Maisel Licerán, S. H. Boeve, And H. T. C. Stoof

We study dilute two-dimensional systems of interacting excitons with a moat dispersion, whose ground-state manifold consists of a set of discrete or continuously degenerate energy minima. At low densities and in the presence of contact interactions, it is known that the bosons can undergo statistica…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065409] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies correlated phases of moat-band excitons in two dimensions, focusing on statistical transmutation and topological phases.
motivation: To understand the low-density behavior of interacting bosons with a moat dispersion, which can lead to exotic quantum phases.
method: The authors use field-theoretic methods to analyze the system, including the effects of contact interactions and statistical transmutation.
result: They find that the system can undergo statistical transmutation, leading to phases with anyonic statistics and topological order.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the physics of moat-band excitons and their potential for realizing topological phases in two-dimensional systems.

title: Vibrational Spectrum Of Vitreous Silica: Rigorous Decomposition Via Recursive Orthogonal Splitting Analysis
authors: Nikita S. Shcheblanov And Anaël Lemaître
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita S. Shcheblanov and Anaël Lemaître

Our understanding of vibrations in solids currently rests on concepts and techniques designed for crystals and explicitly relying on periodicity, hence inapplicable to amorphous materials. As a consequence, no established framework enables a systematic decomposition of the vibrational spectrum of am…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014205] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to decompose the vibrational spectrum of amorphous silica using recursive orthogonal splitting, addressing a gap in the study of disordered solids.
motivation: Current understanding of vibrations in solids relies on concepts designed for crystals, which are inapplicable to amorphous materials. A systematic framework for decomposing vibrational spectra of glasses is lacking.
method: The authors develop a recursive orthogonal splitting analysis to decompose the vibrational density of states of vitreous silica into contributions from local structural motifs.
result: The method yields a rigorous decomposition of the vibrational spectrum, revealing the contributions of different local environments to the overall density of states.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for analyzing vibrations in amorphous solids, potentially aiding in understanding thermal and mechanical properties of glasses.

title: Magnetic Lock-in Transition And Competing Interactions In EuAuBi
authors: S. H. Moody, C. Ritter, H. Takahashi, S. Ishiwata, And J. S. White

tldr: This paper studies the magnetic ground state of EuAuBi using neutron diffraction, focusing on antiferromagnetic ordering and competing interactions.
motivation: Understanding the magnetic properties of EuAuBi, a superconducting polar semimetal, is important for its potential applications.
method: Neutron powder diffraction was used to determine the zero-field magnetic ground state and magnetic structure.
result: The system exhibits a commensurate antiferromagnetic ground state with a specific wave vector and moment orientation.
conclusion: The magnetic ordering in EuAuBi is characterized, providing insight into its competing interactions.

title: Geometric Flat-band Splitting In The Double-layer Metallic Lieb Lattice
authors: Go Itami And Osamu Sakai
abstract:
Author(s): Go Itami and Osamu Sakai

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045413] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies geometric flat-band splitting in a double-layer metallic Lieb lattice, focusing on band geometry and compact localized states.
motivation: Flat bands are sensitive to weak perturbations and offer a platform for band-geometry engineering; understanding splitting in bilayer systems may enable new phenomena.
method: The authors analyze a double-layer Lieb lattice model, likely using tight-binding or continuum methods to compute band structure and splitting.
result: They observe geometry-tunable splitting of flat bands, analogous to flat-band reconstruction, in a linear-wave context.
conclusion: The work provides insights into band-geometry engineering in bilayer flat-band systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Shot Noise Signatures Identifying non-Abelian Properties Of Jackiw-Rebbi Zero Modes
authors: Haoran Ge, Zhen Chen, Yijia Wu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Haoran Ge, Zhen Chen, Yijia Wu, and X. C. Xie

Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes were first proposed in 1976 as topologically protected zero-energy states localized at domain walls in one-dimensional Dirac systems. They have attracted widespread attention in the field of topological quantum computing, as they serve as nonsuperconducting analogs of Majoran…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055407] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shot noise signatures of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes in one-dimensional Dirac systems, which are topologically protected zero-energy states relevant to topological quantum computing.
motivation: Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes are non-superconducting analogs of Majorana zero modes and could be used for topological quantum computing, but their non-Abelian properties need experimental verification.
method: The authors theoretically analyze shot noise in transport through a junction hosting Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes, identifying signatures that distinguish them from trivial zero modes.
result: They find that the shot noise exhibits specific features, such as a Fano factor of 1/2, that can serve as a fingerprint of the non-Abelian statistics of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes.
conclusion: Shot noise measurements can provide clear experimental signatures to identify non-Abelian properties of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes, aiding in their detection and potential use in topological quantum computing.

title: Dynamical Response Of The Kitaev Spin Liquid Under Third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg Interaction

tldr: This paper studies the dynamical spin structure factor of the Kitaev spin liquid under a third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg perturbation.
motivation: Growing evidence suggests third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg interactions are significant in candidate Kitaev materials, motivating a study of their effect on the Kitaev spin liquid's dynamical properties.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and analytical methods to compute the spin dynamical structure factor of the Kitaev spin liquid with a third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg perturbation.
result: The perturbation induces additional spectral features and modifies the low-energy spin dynamics, including the emergence of new magnon-like modes.
conclusion: The third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg interaction significantly alters the dynamical response of the Kitaev spin liquid, which may help interpret inelastic neutron scattering experiments on candidate materials.

title: Study Of The Triangular-lattice Hubbard Model With Constrained-path Quantum Monte Carlo
authors: Shu Fay Ung, Ankit Mahajan, And David R. Reichman

tldr: Benchmarks constrained-path quantum Monte Carlo on the triangular-lattice Hubbard model, focusing on improving trial wave functions for quantitative accuracy.
motivation: The triangular-lattice Hubbard model is a challenging strongly correlated system; accurate numerical methods are needed to understand its phase diagram.
method: Constrained-path quantum Monte Carlo (CPMC) with symmetry-adapted trial wave functions is used to simulate the model at various fillings and interaction strengths.
result: Symmetry-adapted trial wave functions significantly improve the accuracy of CPMC compared to free-electron-based trials, especially away from half filling.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that improved trial states enhance CPMC performance, providing a reliable benchmark for the triangular-lattice Hubbard model.

title: Tunable Topology, Hall Response, And Spin Textures In Bicircularly Polarized Light Illuminated Altermagnets

tldr: This paper studies the effect of bicircularly polarized light on altermagnets, focusing on tunable topology, Hall response, and spin textures.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit nonrelativistic spin splitting, and controlling their topological and spin properties via light is of interest for spintronics.
method: The authors theoretically investigate altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling under bicircularly polarized light, likely using tight-binding or continuum models.
result: They discover remarkable tunability of topology, Hall response, and spin textures.
conclusion: Bicircularly polarized light provides a means to control topological and spin properties in altermagnets.

title: Anomalous Transport In Quasiperiodic Lattices: Emergent Exceptional Points At Band Edges And Log-periodic Oscillations
authors: Jinyuan Shang And Haiping Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyuan Shang and Haiping Hu

Quasiperiodic systems host exotic transport regimes that are distinct from those found in periodic or disordered lattices. In this work, we study quantum transport in the Aubry-André-Harper lattice in a two-terminal setup coupled to zero-temperature reservoirs, where the conductance is evaluated via…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous transport in quasiperiodic lattices, focusing on emergent exceptional points and log-periodic oscillations.
motivation: To understand quantum transport in quasiperiodic systems, which exhibit exotic regimes distinct from periodic or disordered lattices.
method: The authors study the Aubry-André-Harper lattice in a two-terminal setup coupled to zero-temperature reservoirs and evaluate conductance.
result: They find emergent exceptional points at band edges and log-periodic oscillations in transport properties.
conclusion: The work reveals new transport phenomena in quasiperiodic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Supercurrent-induced Phonon Angular Momentum

tldr: This paper studies supercurrent-induced phonon angular momentum in mixed parity and d-wave superconductors, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: To understand the generation of phonon angular momentum via supercurrents in unconventional superconductors.
method: Perturbative calculation to derive analytical expressions for phonon angular momentum induced by supercurrent.
result: Analytical expressions for phonon angular momentum are obtained, with physical interpretation provided.
conclusion: Supercurrent can induce phonon angular momentum in certain superconductors, offering a new mechanism for angular momentum transfer.

title: Low-temperature Anomaly And Anisotropy Of Critical Magnetic Fields In Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Superconductors
authors: Tomoya Sano, Kota Tabata, Akihiro Sasaki, And Yasuhiro Asano

tldr: This paper explains the persistence of spin-singlet superconductivity in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides under high magnetic fields due to Ising protection.
motivation: To understand why superconductivity survives beyond the Pauli limit in these materials, which is a condensed matter physics problem.
method: The authors analyze the interplay between Zeeman field and Ising spin-orbit interaction using theoretical modeling.
result: They clarify the mechanism of Ising protection and show how it leads to anisotropic critical magnetic fields.
conclusion: The findings explain the low-temperature anomaly in critical fields but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Anisotropic Heisenberg Model Close To The Ising Limit: Triangular Lattice Versus Effective Models
authors: M. Ulaga, J. Kokalj, T. Tohyama, And P. Prelovšek

Stimulated by recent experiments on materials representing the realization of the anisotropic Heisenberg spin-[MATH] model on a triangular lattice (TL), we explore further properties of such a model in the easy-axis regime [MATH] and the plausibility of finding effective models that…

tldr: This paper studies the anisotropic Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice near the Ising limit, focusing on effective models and properties like magnetization and specific heat.
motivation: Recent experiments on materials realizing the anisotropic Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice motivate a deeper theoretical exploration of its properties and the validity of effective models.
method: The authors use numerical methods (likely exact diagonalization or Monte Carlo) to compute thermodynamic quantities and compare the full model with effective Ising-like models.
result: They find that effective models capture some features but fail to reproduce certain low-temperature properties, indicating the importance of quantum fluctuations.
conclusion: The study highlights limitations of simplified effective models for the anisotropic Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice, suggesting that full quantum treatment is necessary for accurate description.

title: Apparent Double ${T}_{c}$ From A Single Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition In Anisotropic Phase-only Models
authors: Pei-Yuan Cai And Yi Zhou
abstract:

To establish a baseline, we study a minimal anisotropic phase-o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034505] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic phase-only models and shows that a single Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition can produce an apparent double transition temperature in transport experiments.
motivation: Transport experiments on two-dimensional superconductors often show direction-dependent transition temperatures, and the authors aim to determine whether this reflects a true thermodynamic splitting or a transport artifact.
method: The authors analyze a minimal anisotropic phase-only model using renormalization group methods and calculate the superfluid stiffness and transport properties.
result: They find that a single BKT transition can yield an apparent double Tc due to anisotropy in the phase stiffness, without any thermodynamic splitting.
conclusion: The apparent double Tc is a transport artifact, not a true thermodynamic phase transition, which resolves a puzzle in experimental observations.

title: Stripe Spin-density Wave And Chiral Superconductivity In $t{\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$
